segments.line: Hour twenty- five. Eight in the morning. Light is now slower than Usain Bolt.
He ran a hundred meters in nine point five eight seconds. That's real.
Today, light would lose that race.
There's no sunrise. Just a black sky and frost on every window.
Then a man in a suit walks down the middle of your street with a megaphone.
Shouting is suddenly the fastest way to tell people anything.
Sound beats light now.
'Listen to me. The government is opening shelters underground.
Subway tunnels. Mines. Parking garages.
Buses to the shelter leave the station at noon. '
Why underground? A few meters under the surface, the ground stays about the same temperature all year round.
Summer or winter, sun or no sun. That's real.
Down there, people can survive the cold.
Across the city, the same speech is being shouted on every street corner, by soldiers, teachers, and bus drivers.
Ellie tugs at the man's sleeve. 'Can my cat come? '
He looks down at her for a long moment. 'Yes, ' he says. 'The cat can come. '
Mo's dad asks
the question everybody is thinking. 'Is there room for everyone? ' The man in the suit doesn't answer. He just lowers his megaphone.
'Be at the station by noon. The buses won't wait. '
Then you remember.
Your mom works the night shift at the hospital, across town. She never came home this morning.
Her phone doesn't answer, because every message now crawls.
It's three kilometers to the hospital, and the buses leave at noon.
